images.title: Half and fourth of chikki
images.purpose: Show that Meena's half is 2 fourths, so with her brother's 1 fourth they ate 3 fourths of the chikki.
images.composition: One long chikki bar in the upper middle with wide margins, and one sum line centred below it.
images.exact_structure: One long flat rectangular chikki bar cut by straight lines into 4 equal pieces. From the left: pieces 1 and 2 filled teal #0072B2, piece 3 filled amber #E69F00, piece 4 plain. A thin reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket above pieces 1 and 2 marks Meena's half; a smaller bracket above piece 3 marks her brother's share. Centred below the bar: one sum line. Exactly 1 bar, 4 equal pieces, 2 teal, 1 amber, 1 plain.

images.takeaway: See the half as 2 fourths, then count the fourths.
images.description: One chikki bar in 4 equal pieces: 2 teal pieces are Meena's 1/2 = 2/4 and 1 amber piece is her brother's 1/4, so together they ate 3/4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the coloured fourths aloud: one, two, three fourths.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the half as two fourths on one bar is the whole idea; one clean image carries it.
